description: Anti-money laundering, counter-terrorism financing, counter-proliferation financing, sanctions. Spans banking, payments, crypto, real-estate, legal, accounting, gambling, and high-value-dealer sectors.

regulatory_bodies.name: US Office of Foreign Assets Control
Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada
Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre
Conselho de Controle de Atividades Financeiras

regulations.name: FATF Recommendations on AML/CFT
regulations.summary: 40 Recommendations setting the global AML/CFT/CPF standard, adopted into national law by FATF members (200+ jurisdictions via FATF-style regional bodies).
key_requirements: Enhanced due diligence for higher-risk customers and PEPs

regulations.name: OFAC Economic Sanctions Programs
regulations.extra_territorial_scope: US persons globally; non-US persons with US-nexus transactions (USD clearing, US tech, US persons involved). Secondary sanctions reach further.
regulations.summary: Sanctions programs with wide extra-territorial reach through USD clearing and US secondary sanctions.
key_requirements: Screen counterparties against the SDN list and sector-specific lists
Block transactions and property of designated parties
Report blocked property and rejected transactions
Maintain a sanctions compliance programme (OFAC Framework for Compliance Commitments)

regulations.name: Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds Regulations 2017
regulations.summary: UK implementation of FATF standards. Amended 2022 to cover cryptoasset firms.
key_requirements: EDD for PEPs and higher-risk relationships
Record-keeping for 5 years after relationship ends

regulations.name: Bank Secrecy Act / AML regime
regulations.issuing_body: US Congress (1970); amended by USA PATRIOT Act (2001), AML Act of 2020
regulations.summary: Principal US AML framework. AML Act 2020 introduced beneficial ownership reporting via Corporate Transparency Act.
key_requirements: AML programme — internal controls, training, independent testing, compliance officer

regulations.name: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act
key_requirements: Compliance programme — policies, risk assessment, training, independent review

regulations.name: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006
regulations.summary: Australia's AML/CTF framework. Tranche 2 extensions to lawyers, accountants, real estate, trust/company service providers effective 2026.
key_requirements: AML/CTF programme — Part A (enterprise-wide) and Part B (CDD)
Ongoing due diligence and transaction monitoring

regulations.name: Anti-Money Laundering Act (Switzerland)
regulations.summary: Swiss AML framework. Amended 2023 to strengthen beneficial ownership transparency.
key_requirements: Financial intermediary affiliation with FINMA-supervised body or SRO
Identification of contracting party and beneficial owner
Ongoing due diligence and risk-based approach

regulations.name: DFSA Rulebook — Anti-Money Laundering Module (AML)
regulations.summary: AML/CFT rules for DIFC authorised firms — FATF-aligned.
key_requirements: Suspicious activity reporting to the FIU

regulations.name: Brazil — Money Laundering Law (Law 9,613/1998)
regulations.summary: Core Brazilian AML legislation. Sector-specific rules via BACEN Circular 3,978 and CVM Resolution 50.
key_requirements: Transaction monitoring and STRs to COAF
